summary:
T.U.L.I.P
Thermal  sUrvelliance of Landscape Ignition Patterns
An interactive satellite-based hotspot activity monitoring and historical data analysis platform.

The platform combines the data from both VIIRS (NOAA-20/NOAA-21/SUOMI SNPP) and MODIS (Terra/Aqua) satellites while taking into consideration the differences between two systems to explore anomalies and recurring patterns. 
The project combines geospatial visualisation, historical analysis and an experimental statistical forecasting system.

Note: The backend API is implemented and deployed. The frontend integration is currently under development and may not yet provide full functionality.
details:
THE PROBLEM

Although satellite fire detection data is publicly available, interpreting historical activity across selected regions and time periods and finding underlying patterns requires additional work.

T.U.L.I.P. aims to make such an analysis more accessible by featuring a user-friendly interface and interactive statistical tools.

MAIN FEATURES

- Hotspot visualisation

- Historical quantities of hotspots

- Historical FRP quantities of hotspots

- Grid View visualisation (backend implemented)

- Experimental monthly forecast

FORECASTING METHODOLOGY

T.U.L.I.P. utilises a Generalised Linear Model with Tweedie distribution and Fourier transform based seasonal patterns.

The model represents the expected total FRP (Fire Radiative Power) values.


TECH STACK

Frontend

The Unity Engine (formerly)

Cesium.js

Backend

Python libraries (specified in requirements.txt)

PostgreSQL
